entities.name: Marcus Manilius
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Manilius was a Roman poet and astrologer of the early Imperial period, best known as the author of the Astronomica, a didactic poem in five books that expounds Hellenistic astrology in Latin hexameters. Almost nothing is securely known of his life: he is not mentioned by contemporary authors, and modern dating rests on internal references that place composition under Augustus and into the reign of Tiberius (early 1st century CE). The Astronomica treats the celestial sphere, the zodiac, the influences of the signs and planets, and the casting of horoscopes, weaving Stoic cosmology with technical astrological doctrine.

As a literary and intellectual document, the poem is a principal Latin witness to the systematisation of astrology in the Roman world after the late Republic, when Greek mathematical astronomy and Chaldaean star lore were absorbed into elite culture. Manilius presents the cosmos as a rationally ordered, fate-governing whole, and his verse both popularises and elevates technical material for educated readers. Though incomplete or uneven in places, the Astronomica remained a key source for later Latin astrology and for modern reconstruction of ancient horoscopic practice.
